title: Human impact on ecosystems
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What are some ways humans harm natural habitats?
How does pollution affect animal life?
Can we really fix the damage from deforestation?

explain.say: Today we look at how humans impact nature.
Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances into the environment.
Deforestation means cutting down large areas of trees for human use.
Peatlands are waterlogged soil formed from decaying vegetation over time.
When we drain peatlands, the stored carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere.
In daily life, plastic pollution in our oceans is a clear example of human impact.

faq.q: What is the difference between pollution and waste?
faq.a: Pollution refers to the introduction of harmful substances. Waste is the discarded material itself. You could also ask: What makes something polluting? Or: Is trash always pollution?
asks: Is litter the same as pollution?
What is the source of pollution?

faq.q: Why is deforestation so bad for biodiversity?
faq.a: Deforestation removes the physical space where many species live. This loss of habitat can cause species to become extinct. You might ask: How does cutting trees hurt animals? Or: What is the impact of losing forests?
asks: What happens when we cut down forests?

faq.q: How does draining peatlands affect the climate?
faq.a: Draining peatlands exposes the stored organic matter to air. This allows it to decompose and release large amounts of carbon dioxide. Another way to ask is: What is the carbon cycle connection to peat? Or: Does peat decay release gas?
asks: What gases come out of wet peat?
Why is peatland drainage a climate issue?

faq.q: What is the best way to reduce pollution?
faq.a: Reducing pollution requires changing our energy sources and habits. We can use less fossil fuels and manage waste better. You could also ask: What are sustainable practices? Or: How can we clean up pollution?

facts: Air pollution often comes from burning fossil fuels like petrol.
Deforestation reduces the amount of oxygen produced by plants.
Peatlands are vital carbon sinks, meaning they store large amounts of carbon.
Plastic pollution breaks down into smaller pieces called microplastics.

quiz.say: Which activity primarily contributes to air pollution?
quiz.why: Burning gasoline releases harmful gases into the air.

wrong.1: Planting trees absorb carbon dioxide, which is helpful.
wrong.2: Filtering water cleans pollutants from liquids.
wrong.3: Solar power generates electricity without burning fuels.

quiz.say: What is the main ecological consequence of deforestation?
quiz.why: Trees provide homes for countless species, so removing them causes habitat loss.

wrong.0: Forests help regulate local rainfall patterns.
wrong.1: Leaf litter helps keep the soil rich in nutrients.
wrong.2: Forests act as carbon sinks, cooling the planet.

quiz.say: If peatlands are drained, what happens to their stored carbon?
quiz.show: It is released as carbon dioxide

options.show: It is released as carbon dioxide
options.say: It is released as carbon dioxide

quiz.why: When waterlogged peat dries, microbes break it down, releasing stored carbon.

wrong.1: The carbon is released into the atmosphere, not absorbed.
wrong.2: Draining the peat exposes it to oxygen, causing decomposition.
wrong.3: While methane is released, the primary, large-scale release is as carbon dioxide.
